create.name: Dr. Kristin Neff
create.bio:
Kristin Neff is the researcher who first defined self-compassion as something that could be measured and studied, and she has since become one of its best-known teachers. She came to it through Buddhist practice in her last year of graduate school at Berkeley, then built a theory and a scale during her postdoctoral years and spent her academic career at the University of Texas at Austin. Together with Chris Germer she created Mindful Self-Compassion, an eight-week course for the general public, and co-founded the non-profit Center for Mindful Self-Compassion.

She describes self-compassion as three linked capacities: kindness toward oneself, a sense of shared humanity, and mindful awareness of pain without being swept away by it. Her later work adds a fierce side, the energy to protect oneself, speak up and act, alongside the tender side of comfort and acceptance. Having left university life, she now runs the Self-Compassion Institute from Austin, Texas, where a paid online community offers her monthly gatherings, guest conversations and a short introductory course, and mentors teach a six-week foundations class. Her books include Self-Compassion and Fierce Self-Compassion, and she offers many free guided practices on her site.

books.title: Self-Compassion: The Proven Power of Being Kind to Yourself
books.author: Kristin Neff
books.description: Her first book for general readers. It explains the three parts of self-compassion, draws on her research and her own family life, and includes exercises for treating yourself as you would a good friend.

books.title: Fierce Self-Compassion: How Women Can Harness Kindness to Speak Up, Claim Their Power, and Thrive
books.author: Kristin Neff
books.description: Adds an active side to her earlier work: protecting yourself, meeting your own needs and pushing for change, balanced with gentler acceptance. It includes practices for each.

books.title: The Mindful Self-Compassion Workbook: A Proven Way to Accept Yourself, Build Inner Strength, and Thrive
books.author: Kristin Neff, Christopher Germer
books.description: A self-guided version of the eight-week MSC course, written with Chris Germer. Each chapter pairs a short explanation with meditations and informal exercises a reader can work through alone.

books.title: Teaching the Mindful Self-Compassion Program: A Guide for Professionals
books.author: Christopher Germer, Kristin Neff
books.description: A detailed handbook for people training to teach MSC, written with Chris Germer. It sets out the course session by session along with the thinking behind it.

courses.title: Self-Compassion Community membership
courses.description: An online membership run by her institute. It includes her monthly live gatherings with a short practice and questions, conversations with guest teachers, a one-hour introductory course, a library of guided practices and drop-in sessions with mentors.

courses.title: Foundations of Self-Compassion (6-week online course)
courses.description: A shorter, nine-hour version of the Mindful Self-Compassion programme, taught live on Zoom over six weekly sessions by mentors from her institute. It comes with six months of community membership.

free_resources.title: General Self-Compassion Break
free_resources.description: A five-minute recorded practice that brings mindfulness, a sense of shared humanity and kindness to whatever is hard right now.

free_resources.title: Affectionate Breathing
free_resources.description: An 18-minute guided breath meditation done with a warm, friendly attitude toward yourself.

free_resources.title: Fierce Friend
free_resources.description: A guided visualisation of meeting an inner ally who is both caring and strong, to find courage for something you need to do.

free_resources.title: Loving-Kindness Meditation
free_resources.description: A twenty-minute version of traditional loving-kindness practice, adapted to help you wish yourself well.

free_resources.title: Compassionate Body Scan
free_resources.description: A guided scan through the body that brings appreciation and kindness to each part in turn.
